applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (1999), as replaced/para el régimen de la Ley 18/2020? No

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 19-22, 29, 60-64, 124-129 and 209-210
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central for name reservation; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for inscription
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed) executed before a notary, together with Modelo 036 and the Registro Mercantil presentation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation. The capital must be deposited in a blocked account at a Spanish credit institution or directly with the Notary using the Caja General de Depósitos mechanism; the deposit is released only upon registration in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned promoters and sole shareholders, acting at the inaugural General Meeting, hereby resolve: (1) The company is validly incorporated under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital; (2) The share capital of EUR 3,000 is subscribed and fully paid by the shareholders as shown in the public deed; (3) The registered office is fixed at [address, province] and the deed of incorporation shall state this domicile; (4) [Name] is appointed as Sole Administrator and accepts the appointment; (5) The administrator is authorized to complete the provisional NIF application, Registro Mercantil registration, municipal licenses, and all ancillary filings for the commencement of operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate from Registro Mercantil Central
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, online via the Colegio de Registradores portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a telematic application for a certificación de denominación social with up to three proposed company names. The Registry checks name availability and issues a certificate valid for three months. Confirm the exact legal form 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada'.
required_dossiers: List of three proposed company names in order of preference
Identification of each promoter (NIE/passport or DNI for Spanish residents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If one or all proposed names are rejected due to similarity or inadmissibility, resubmit a new application with fresh alternatives. A formal refusal may be appealed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Provisional Bank Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a 'cuenta corriente de constitución' in the name of the company under formation and deposit at least EUR 3,000. Obtain a certificate from the bank stating the amount, account number, and that the funds are blocked until the company is registered in the Registro Mercantil.
required_dossiers: Name certificate issued by Registro Mercantil Central
Identity documents and tax identification numbers of the promoters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account opening for anti-money-laundering reasons, provide enhanced due diligence documents or choose another credit institution. Alternatively, deposit the capital with the notary through the Caja General de Depósitos.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the district where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, draft by-laws, and personal data of directors to the notary. The notary verifies legality, reads the deed, and obtains signatures from all shareholders. The deed will include the company name, corporate purpose, capitalization, registered office, and administration rules. The notary will request a provisional NIF from the Agencia Tributaria simultaneously.
required_dossiers: NIE/passport of all shareholders and directors
Contact and postal addresses of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the document, the shareholders must rectify and sign a corrected deed. A notarial refusal must be reasoned and may be appealed through notarial disciplinary procedures or by using a different notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay AJD Transfer Tax and Apply for Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) – territorial delegation corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty business days from the deed, self-assess the 'Actos Jurídicos Documentados' (AJD) tax using Modelo 600 and obtain the stamped copy. Then file Modelo 036 with AEAT to obtain the definitive NIF, providing the public deed and proof of AJD payment.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries missing information or tax self-assessment errors, submit a corrective declaration and pay any applicable surcharge. Late filing is subject to late-payment penalties and can be mitigated by timely voluntary correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial 'testimonio' and an authorized copy of the public deed to the Registro Mercantil Provincial, together with proof of NIF and paid AJD. The Registrar examines the legality of the deed and issues the inscription; once registered, the SL acquires legal personality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a suspensive qualification, correct the defects and resubmit within the granted period. A final refusal may be appealed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax Census, Economic Activity, and Employer Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the entrepreneur census (Censo de Empresarios) through Modelo 036 if not already done; file the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) declaration for manufacturing activity; register as an employer with TGSS using the RED system and obtain workplace accident insurance if employees will be hired.
required_dossiers: Form Modelo 036 with IAE tax assignment
Company tax identification and bank account
Employment contract templates and accident insurance policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or distracted, file the missing declaration and pay any proportional surcharge. For TGSS delays, follow the administrative reassignment procedure and request a clear resale of the effective date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería competente en materia de industria y comercio de la Comunidad Autónoma, and the Ayuntamiento where the manufacturing workshop is located
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento or Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad (depending on the municipal ordinance for small workshop facilities)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Department of the Regional Government (e.g. Consejería de Medio Ambiente) and, where applicable, the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No full EIA required for small-scale artisan casting; subject to simple environmental communication/municipal activity registration under Ley 21/2013 and Ley 34/2007 due to VOC-emitting epoxy resin operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer must comply with local discharge limits; VOC emissions must remain below the thresholds requiring an environmental operating permit; hazardous waste (epoxy residues, solvents, uncontaminated packaging) must be handled and disposed by an authorized waste manager with documented waste manifests; occupational exposure limits under the INSST VLA list and REACH/CLP labeling obligations apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Required fire safety certificate from the local fire service, low-voltage electrical installation inspection certificate, structural load clearance for equipment racks and molds, and a workplace health-and-safety compliance declaration from an accredited Prevención de Riesgos Laborales service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF upon incorporation via notary and Mercantile Registry filing; foreign entities register for NIE and NIF if establishing permanent establishment or conducting taxable activity in Spain; VAT identification number (NIF prefixed with ES) assigned post-registration with AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include simplified tax regime for SMEs, fiscal consolidation groups, and hybrid mismatch adjustments under EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD); entity-level taxation remains default with territorial scope options for qualifying activities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 50,000 EUR annual turnover threshold triggering mandatory registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance via SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) with mandatory digital stamping and API integration for large taxpayers; all invoices require AEAT-compliant digital format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported outside the EU or qualifying offshore services; eligibility requires proof of actual export and non-EU destination
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims subject to 100% penalty surcharge, interest accrual, and potential criminal prosecution; retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT with possible loss of VAT registration and export privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national competent authority, operating within the Eurosystem framework under the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and foreign exchange operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange control restrictions on capital movements, profit remittances, or dividend distributions to non-residents, subject to standard corporate tax and withholding tax obligations (e.g., 19% withholding on dividends unless reduced by tax treaty). Current account transactions (trade, services, transfers) are unrestricted. Capital account operations (foreign direct investment, loans, securities) require only statistical reporting to the Banco de España for balance-of-payments purposes, not prior authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirements exist for export proceeds in Spain or the EU. Exporters may retain foreign currency earnings in domestic or foreign bank accounts, convert to EUR at their discretion, or use them for trade settlements. Reporting obligations under the Spanish Balance of Payments (BoP) system apply for statistical purposes, but no timeline or conversion ratio is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente) and Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for fintech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the Spanish E-Money Law (Ley 21/2011). Entities such as N26, Revolut, and Qonto operate in Spain and offer multi-currency accounts, SWIFT/SEPA transfers, and FX services. Legal constraints include: (i) EMIs cannot provide credit or hold client funds as deposits; (ii) they must be licensed in an EU/EEA state and passport into Spain; (iii) for high-volume trade settlements, traditional banks may offer more robust correspondent banking relationships. For a low-risk manufacturing entity, EMIs are viable for operational liquidity but may not support complex trade finance instruments (e.g., LC issuance).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For corporate account opening, Spanish banks generally require at least one director or authorized signatory to appear physically for identity verification, especially for non-resident entities. Remote onboarding is permitted for certain banks (e.g., BBVA, Santander) using video identification and digital signatures, but enhanced due diligence may trigger an in-person interview at the bank's discretion. For a Spanish SL with non-resident shareholders, the managing director (administrador) must typically attend a branch meeting or complete a notarized power of attorney (poder) for a local representative. Remote opening is possible but subject to higher scrutiny and longer processing times.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners with high-risk jurisdiction ties (e.g., tax havens or sanctioned countries)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) certified copies of passports and proof of address; (ii) corporate registry extracts (Certificado de Registro Mercantil) showing ultimate beneficial ownership; (iii) tax residency certificates (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the owner's jurisdiction; (iv) a detailed business plan and source-of-funds declaration; (v) audited financial statements or bank references from the home country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., rapid inbound capital injection followed by immediate outbound payments to third parties)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (i) notarized shareholder resolution authorizing the capital injection; (ii) underlying commercial contracts (purchase orders, invoices) for outbound disbursements; (iii) bank statements showing the source of funds; (iv) a cash-flow forecast and explanation of the business cycle; (v) compliance with Spanish BoP reporting (Form BE-1) for the capital movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk product category (e.g., gaming accessories) misinterpreted as gambling-related
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) product catalog and manufacturing process description confirming non-gambling nature; (ii) trademark and IP registrations; (iii) sales platform agreements (Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal) demonstrating legitimate e-commerce; (iv) industry association membership (e.g., Tabletop Gaming Association); (v) a legal opinion from a Spanish attorney confirming the product is not regulated under gambling laws.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Use SWIFT MT103 for international transfers. For equity injections from non-resident shareholders, the purpose code must be 'P01' (Direct Investment – Equity) under the Spanish BoP classification. The receiving bank will require a copy of the notarized capital increase deed (Escritura de Aumento de Capital) and the shareholder resolution. Funds must be credited to the SL's capital escrow account (Cuenta de Depósito) before registration with the Mercantile Registry. Verification: The bank will issue a certificate of receipt (Certificado de Ingreso) for the notary. For loans, use purpose code 'P02' (Loans) and provide a loan agreement. All inbound transfers are subject to BoP statistical reporting (Form BE-1) within 15 days of the transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to suppliers, with purpose codes such as 'P03' (Imports of goods) or 'P04' (Imports of services); (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) issued via SWIFT MT700, typically through the SL's bank (issuing bank) to the beneficiary's bank (advising/confirming bank). For EU suppliers, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is available for EUR payments under €100,000. For non-EU suppliers, SWIFT is mandatory. All outbound payments require underlying commercial invoices and customs declarations (if goods) to satisfy AML and BoP reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (non-deliverable and deliverable) with maturities up to 12 months, available from tier-1 banks for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major pairs.
Currency Swaps (FX Swaps) for simultaneous spot and forward transactions, used for liquidity management.
FX Options (European-style) for hedging contingent exposures, though less common for small entities.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for long-term debt or investment hedging, subject to bank credit approval.

NDFs (Non-Deliverable Forwards) are permissible but rarely used for EUR as the euro is freely convertible; they may be considered for exotic currency exposures (e.g., Latin American currencies) where convertibility is restricted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval by the General Shareholders' Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 300000 EUR and potential administrative dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 days after the end of the tax year (e.g. 25 January for calendar year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 100 EUR per day, interest on unpaid taxes, and possible tax reassessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership or corporate structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and sanctions for non-compliance with UBO registration obligations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Net turnover exceeding 2000000 EUR or total assets exceeding 1000000 EUR in the preceding financial year
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) pursuant to Royal Decree 1514/2007

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Companies must maintain an updated UBO register in the Registro Mercantil; annual updates required upon any change in UBO or corporate structure with filing within one month

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-500 USD annually for registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2000-15000 USD if audit is required based on statutory thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate for the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions. Qualifying start-up companies may also apply a 15% rate during the applicable incentive period. Additional reduced rates may apply to qualifying micro-enterprises and other specially regulated entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The standard rate is 25%. Qualifying newly incorporated entities and qualifying start-ups may apply 15% under the applicable conditions. Tax credits may apply for research and development, technological innovation, cinematographic and audiovisual productions, employment-related measures, and other statutory investments. Accelerated depreciation and other deductions may be available to qualifying small enterprises. Dividends and capital gains from qualifying substantial shareholdings may benefit from the participation exemption, generally subject to a 5% minimum participation and a one-year holding requirement, with a statutory limitation reducing the exemption to 95% in ordinary cases. Spain has no general tax holiday for an ordinary Spanish SL.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Spanish Corporate Income Tax return and non-resident income tax return for permanent establishments, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate or other permitted identification method.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the ordinary filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the last day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing rule extends the deadline to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered office, tax period, legal form, economic activity codes, and tax-group status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the Spanish SL as taxpayer. The SL reports its own NIF, Spanish registered office, resident status, and Spanish tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss shown in the approved statutory accounts before Corporate Income Tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Spanish-accounting results prepared under the Spanish General Accounting Plan. Foreign-parent accounting figures must be reconciled to the Spanish statutory accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive or negative adjustments for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairments, exempt income, tax credits, related-party adjustments, and other Corporate Income Tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude shareholder-level expenses that do not relate to the Spanish SL. Document cross-border management fees, royalties, financing costs, and shared costs as arm's-length and commercially supported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of available tax losses subject to percentage utilization limits, minimum utilization thresholds, anti-avoidance rules, and the statutory indefinite carryforward regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify continuity of ownership and business activity where losses are used following an acquisition. Retain historical returns, accounting records, and evidence that the losses arose in the Spanish taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax base and gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base after adjustments and losses, applicable tax rate, and gross Corporate Income Tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary Spanish rate unless a documented statutory incentive applies. Treaty relief does not reduce the Spanish SL's resident Corporate Income Tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax credits, deductions, withholding credits, foreign-tax credits, and other legally available reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax credits require evidence of payment and income attribution. Do not claim a parent-company foreign tax credit in the SL unless the Spanish rules specifically permit it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments made through Modelo 202 and any withholding or payment-on-account credits attributable to the Spanish SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all Modelo 202 payments and third-party withholding certificates to the annual return. A non-resident owner cannot use the owner's withholding certificates in the SL's return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance after credits and payments on account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made from an accepted Spanish or SEPA payment route. Refund claims require accurate bank-account details and supporting reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions, transaction categories, amounts, counterparties, valuation methods, and applicable documentation status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transactions with foreign shareholders, group entities, directors, controlled distributors, licensors, financiers, and centralized service companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, changes in equity, cash-flow information where required, and reconciliation to the tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign consolidated accounts do not replace the Spanish SL's statutory accounts. Use consistent functional currency conversion and preserve source documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT request generally triggers a voluntary-period surcharge of 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay, subject to a 12% maximum before the statutory post-12-month regime. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15%, plus late-payment interest from the end of the 12-month period. A fixed penalty may apply where no tax is payable or where the return is filed after an AEAT request. Incorrect returns may generate tax underpayment penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount, depending on concealment and aggravating factors. Voluntary correction before an audit may reduce exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Corporate Income Tax payment on account, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment dates; generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December, with the final electronic payment-day rule extending the deadline where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Payments are generally due from 1 to 20 April, 1 to 20 October, and 1 to 20 December. The calculation is normally based either on the preceding year's tax liability or on the current year's accounting tax base, depending on the statutory method applicable to the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, legal name, tax period, and applicable payment-on-account method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files under its own NIF. Foreign ownership does not eliminate the payment-on-account obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year Corporate Income Tax liability or current-period tax base, as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude amounts attributable solely to the foreign shareholder and reconcile the calculation to Spanish books and filed returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory percentage applied to the relevant basis, reduced by permitted credits and prior payments where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the calculation file, ledger extracts, and evidence of payment for each installment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally triggers a 1% surcharge plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months, and generally 15% after 12 months, in addition to applicable interest after the statutory period. Failure to file or materially incorrect filing can result in fixed penalties or tax underpayment penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, related-party transaction and tax-haven information statement, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters when statutory thresholds or transaction categories are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the ordinary period is November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counterparty, country, relationship category, transaction type, amount, and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including financing, licensing, services, procurement, distribution, and shareholder transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregated amounts by transaction type and counterparty, together with transactions subject to special reporting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use consistent aggregation with the Local File and statutory books. Do not split economically connected transactions to avoid reporting thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions and holdings involving jurisdictions included in applicable Spanish non-cooperative or equivalent statutory lists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm current Spanish lists at the filing date and retain beneficial-ownership and substance evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, or incomplete or inaccurate reporting may generate fixed penalties under the General Tax Law and may increase audit risk, especially where the omitted information concerns related-party transactions or low-tax jurisdictions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident recipient, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or EEA parent may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A qualifying participation generally requires at least 5% ownership or the applicable statutory acquisition-value test and a one-year holding period, which may be completed after payment if security requirements are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its competent foreign tax authority before payment, together with beneficial-owner, ownership, holding-period, legal-form, and anti-abuse evidence. The Spanish payer normally applies the treaty or domestic exemption at source only when documentation is sufficient; otherwise it withholds 19% and the recipient may seek a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax procedure. Treaty rates depend on the relevant bilateral treaty and commonly reduce dividend withholding to 5% or 15%, with variations for substantial corporate participations. A tax-residence certificate should generally be renewed according to its validity period and retained with the payment file.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish domestic withholding is generally 24% for non-residents outside the EU or EEA and 19% for residents of qualifying EU or EEA jurisdictions, subject to statutory conditions and exclusions. Interest and royalty payments to qualifying associated companies in EU Member States may be exempt under the Interest and Royalties Directive implementation if minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse requirements are met. Tax treaties frequently reduce interest or royalty withholding to 0% or 5% to 10%, but the applicable treaty must be checked separately. Spanish-source income characterization, beneficial ownership, permanent-establishment attribution, and anti-abuse rules remain decisive.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The principal Spanish Local File exemption threshold is generally EUR 250,000 of controlled transactions of the same type with the same related party during the tax period, subject to transaction-category exclusions and special documentation rules. Documentation may still be required below that amount for certain transactions, including transfers of businesses or shares, transfers of real estate, and transfers of intangible assets. The Master File is generally relevant where the Spanish entity belongs to a multinational group required to prepare it; the EUR 750 million consolidated-group threshold principally determines Country-by-Country Reporting obligations, not a universal Master File exemption.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the prescribed methods cannot reliably be applied
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate United Arab Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is nevertheless relevant under Spanish anti-abuse rules, the Principal Purpose Test where applicable under a treaty, beneficial-ownership requirements, the EU anti-abuse framework, controlled foreign company rules, the interest limitation regime, hybrid mismatch rules, and the general prohibition of simulation and tax fraud. The Spanish SL should maintain real decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity under effective control, premises or operational infrastructure proportionate to its business, Spanish accounting and banking records, inventory and fulfillment evidence, genuine commercial contracts, and director governance. A mere conduit, circular payment flow, artificial royalty, or shareholder-funded arrangement lacking commercial rationale may be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax evasion and concealed income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting sales from Kickstarter, Stripe, PayPal, marketplaces, or cash channels; fabricating expenses; using personal accounts for company receipts; or creating false invoices to reduce the Spanish tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment and aggravating circumstances, in addition to tax, interest, and possible surcharge. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax period may constitute a criminal offence, generally punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases carry higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for intentional or negligent breach of duties, subsidiary tax liability where statutory conditions are met, and criminal liability for deliberate participation. Criminal conviction may produce imprisonment, fines, disqualification, and asset seizure. A general automatic travel ban does not arise solely from a tax assessment; travel restrictions may arise from judicial measures or insolvency proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register or report Spanish VAT, misapplying the EUR 10,000 EU distance-selling threshold, failing to use the One Stop Shop where appropriate, or treating imported dice, resin, molds, and packaging as VAT-free without legal basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, surcharges, and administrative penalties commonly calculated as a percentage of the unpaid or improperly documented amount. Repeated or concealed conduct can create criminal tax exposure where the criminal threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be secondarily liable where they caused or tolerated non-compliance and statutory conditions are satisfied. Criminal liability requires personal participation or legally relevant omission.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, financing margins, procurement charges, or distribution prices to a foreign shareholder or group company without functions-and-risks support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment, corresponding adjustment where available, secondary adjustment, interest assessment, and documentation penalties. Transfer-pricing documentation failures may generate fixed penalties per missing, inaccurate, or incomplete data point, subject to statutory caps; an underpayment may also attract 50% to 150% penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil or subsidiary tax liability for approving artificial arrangements and criminal liability if the conduct forms part of intentional tax fraud. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced merely because the transaction is adjusted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial ownership, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through an entity with no meaningful personnel, decision-making, commercial risk, or beneficial ownership, solely to obtain treaty or EU-directive benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or directive relief, withholding-tax assessment, interest, tax penalties, and possible application of Spanish anti-abuse and simulation rules. Treaty benefits may be denied under the Principal Purpose Test or beneficial-ownership principles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement a conduit structure may face civil damages, subsidiary tax liability, and criminal exposure where fraud thresholds and intent requirements are satisfied. No automatic imprisonment or travel ban follows from a substance challenge alone.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False accounting and forged commercial documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel books, backdating contracts, issuing invoices for non-existent goods, manipulating inventory, or recording personal expenditure as business expenditure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment and penalties may be combined with criminal offences involving falsification of commercial documents, accounting records, or public documents. Sanctions can include imprisonment, fines, professional disqualification, and confiscation depending on the offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers, and other participants may be personally prosecuted. Civil restitution and compensation claims may attach to responsible individuals. Judicial asset-freezing orders and restrictions on leaving Spain may be imposed where proportionate and ordered by a competent court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or service fees to non-residents without applying, paying, or reporting the required Spanish withholding, or accepting an invalid residence certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish SL may be assessed for the unwithheld amount, late-payment interest, and withholding-related penalties. A payer cannot rely solely on a foreign recipient's informal representation instead of prescribed evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary liability for deliberate or negligent failure to withhold, particularly after an unsuccessful collection process against the company. Criminal liability requires intentional participation and satisfaction of criminal thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party funds, failing to identify beneficial owners, concealing source of funds, structuring payments, or ignoring suspicious transactions involving crowdfunding, payment processors, or crypto-assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may result in public or private reprimands, suspension or removal of responsible officers, and monetary fines that can reach statutory maximums of up to EUR 5 million or a percentage of annual turnover or net worth, depending on the breach and applicable limit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be individually sanctioned, disqualified, or prosecuted for laundering or participation in the underlying offence. Asset confiscation and court-ordered restrictions may apply. A travel ban is not automatic and requires a competent authority or court order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, import, product-safety, and intellectual-property violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring imported resin or finished dice, using incorrect tariff classifications, evading import VAT or customs duty, selling unsafe products, or copying protected game, character, logo, or design rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs debt, import VAT, interest, seizures, administrative fines, destruction or withdrawal of goods, and loss of customs privileges may apply. Serious intellectual-property infringement can result in civil damages and criminal sanctions, including imprisonment in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for deliberate customs fraud, counterfeit trade, or knowing infringement. Civil restitution, injunctions, asset seizure, and criminal disqualification may apply; travel restrictions require judicial authorization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to incur debts while insolvent, preferring connected creditors, diverting company assets, failing to maintain books, or delaying the statutory insolvency filing obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The insolvency may be classified as culpable, with loss of rights against the estate, liability for the insolvency shortfall, return of assets, damages, and disqualification from administering another person's assets for the court-ordered period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto directors may face personal civil liability, asset clawback, disqualification, and, where concealment or asset stripping is criminal, imprisonment and fines. Insolvency courts may impose restrictions affecting travel or asset disposal where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying undeclared wages, misclassifying employees as contractors, diverting company funds to directors, failing to pay social-security contributions, or using company accounts for personal expenditure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Backdated payroll taxes and social-security contributions, surcharges, labour and social-security penalties, tax reassessments, and possible criminal charges for fraud, embezzlement, or unlawful appropriation may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly or subsidiarily liable under applicable tax, social-security, company-law, or criminal provisions. Restitution, disqualification, fines, and imprisonment are possible in serious intentional cases.
